endorsements.quote: When developing fair AI for clinical outcomes, the set of relevant sensitive variables should be carefully re-evaluated for each application with clinical justi fications.
All possible sources of data bias should be proactively identi fied and addressed during the early stages of AI model development before it impedes fair model development.
Clinical AI fairness is a multidisciplinary research topic that requires input from AI researchers, clinicians, and ethicists.

unlisted_practices: Replace race/ethnicity used as a proxy variable with the underlying causal factors where possible.
Investigate the underlying causes of observed subgroup disparities to enable interventions rather than only forcing equal model performance.
Distinguish clinically justified differences from bias and adjust only models with clinically significant bias, avoiding over-adjustment or over-claiming of bias.
Select fairness metrics by accounting for and justifying the ethical implications of group-based versus individual-based fairness in the clinical context.
Define objective, clinically meaningful thresholds to differentiate reasonable subgroup differences from evidence of bias, rather than relying solely on statistical significance.
Adopt equity rather than equality as the objective of clinical AI fairness, incorporating contextual factors such as patient preferences.
Involve clinicians actively across AI model development stages, with two-way communication between clinicians and AI developers, to identify bias and set fairness objectives.
Establish data panels to oversee data collection and avoid data bias.
Incorporate fairness considerations into clinical AI guidelines.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary article discussing considerations and recommendations for translating AI fairness principles into clinical practice.
